problem: Vanilla policy-gradient updates can be too large and unstable, while trust-region optimization is more complex to implement.
contribution: Proximal policy optimization uses a clipped orKL-penalized surrogate and multiple minibatch optimization epochs on collected on-policy data.
algorithm: Estimate advantages from policy rollouts; optimize the minimum of the unclipped probability-ratio advantage and its clipped counterpart. An alternative adapts aKLpenalty. Value and entropy terms depend on the implementation/configuration.
observations: State vectors in continuousMuJoCo benchmarks and visual observations forAtari; privileged simulator state is legitimate for a teacher but not a deployable visualstudent.
actions: Stochastic continuousGaussian or discrete actions depending on the environment.
embodiment_and_data: SevenMuJoCo continuous-control tasks for surrogate comparisons, broader continuous-control andAtari benchmarks. The surrogate study uses3seeds per task and1millionsteps perrun.
experiments: Compare clipping widths, fixed/adaptiveKL, otherRLalgorithms and reward-over-training versus finalreturn. Task reward is not an independently verified real-world successpredicate.
baselines: Unconstrained policygradient, fixed/adaptiveKLvariants,TRPO/A2C/ACER and other context-specific algorithm comparisons.

quantitative_result.note: Source-specific normalization sets randompolicy0andbestresult1; not a physical successrate.

limitations: Clipping is not a hard bound on realizedKL or actuator actions, and no physical safety follows from the surrogate. On-policy sample cost and reward shaping remain significant; later library implementations include additional choices.
hardware_adaptation: Reuse pinnedSB3PPO as the simulated teacher. Report raw action clipping, timestep counts and optimizer updates; a single optimizer smoke test does not mean successful tasklearning.
algorithm_detail: The clipped objective is pessimistic relative to the importance-weighted surrogate and removes incentives for favorable excessive ratios; it does not clip the neural output directly. Multiple epochs reuse the same rollout with advantage estimates. Library advantage/value normalization differences need version-specific provenance.
integration_contract: Record rolloutbuffer size, vectorizedworker count, seed,GAE/discount, actiondistribution, clipping, entropy/value coefficients and actual environment/optimizer counts. Sealed evaluation seeds must differ from training.
license_evidence: The methodpaper is primaryverified. SB3 licensing/version evidence is tracked separately from the original paper and must be pinned before release; no upstream code was copied by this review.
required_experiments: Weightschange after realoptimizer steps; save/reload andresumption equivalence; independentrollout outcomes; throughput/RAM/temperature measurement for1/2/4workers; no privilegedtruth in studentobservations.
difference_from_explorer: PPO is a standardteacher baseline, not evidence of skillmemory or diagnosticnovelty. A CADsimulation model and a trainedteacher require separate validation scopes.
